title: Step of an outward allocation pass
statement: Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a,j\in\mathbb{N}$, and choose a schedule-symbol input, a base configuration, a valid input-head position, integers $b,u$, and tapes $\beta,\mu,\gamma$. Let $i\in\{0,1,2\}$ be an allocation index and choose a direction. Assume the unary tape has a unit marker at $u$ and the guide tape carries the origin mark exactly at coordinate $0$. From allocation index $i$ with guide head at $j$ in the rightward direction or $-j$ in the leftward direction, and with the guide tape filled through $j$ cells in that direction, one step advances the allocation index cyclically, advances the unary head by one exactly when $i=2$, moves the guide head one cell in the chosen direction, and leaves the guide filled through $j+1$ cells.
hypotheses_covered: W is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
base is a configuration on the chosen input
p is a valid input-head position
b and u are integer head positions
bt, ut, and gt are controller tapes
i is an allocation index in {0,1,2}
the unary tape has a unit marker at u
the guide tape has its origin mark exactly at 0
replaced:
Let $\gamma$ be a guide tape carrying the origin mark exactly at cell $0$, and suppose
the unary tape reads a unit marker at the unary head.  Then one step from layout phase
$i$ (of either direction) with guide head at $\pm j$ over the $j$-cell filled version
of $\gamma$ leads to layout phase $i+1 \bmod 3$ with guide head at $\pm(j+1)$ over the
$(j+1)$-cell filled version, incrementing the unary head exactly when $i = 2$.
